versions.agent: Claude Code subagents, same session model in both arms

install.command: claude plugin install frontend-design@claude-plugins-official (or copy SKILL.md)

fixtures: fixtures/12-frontend-design: task/ (README spec for a 6-product pet-food comparison section: species filter, min/max price, 5 sort keys, compare-up-to-3 with sticky bar; data/products.json; synthetic SVG placeholders; serve.mjs; static-only npm test), hidden/ (tests.mjs 4 static + 23 browser tests at 390 and 1280, harness.mjs, slop-markers.mjs, JUDGE.md, judge-pair.mjs, screenshot.mjs), reference/ (1.0), grade.mjs, KEY.md
design: Arm A = plain subagent builds from the spec; Arm B = same prompt + 'read fixtures/skills/frontend-design.SKILL.md first and follow it'. 3 reps per arm, fresh copies. Primary score = 0.6 behaviour + 0.2 axe + 0.2 Lighthouse (script only). Secondary: slop-marker count (script) and a blind pairwise design judge (fixed 3-criterion rubric, random left/right, one fresh judge session per pair, unblinded after all three). Pilot (plain agent) scored 1.0 with 14 slop markers; the task was not hardened further because the score already depends on 27 hidden behaviour/a11y checks and the pilot's weaknesses (slop) are what the skill targets, so the secondary metrics carry the comparison.

candidate_default.config: Arm B with the frontend-design skill
candidate_default.observed: A-1 and B-1 both lost the same 9 filter/sort tests for the same reason: their card CSS sets display on .product-card, which overrides the HTML hidden attribute, so filtered cards stay visible (verified deterministic on regrade; the harness counts visibility, not the attribute). A-1 also had one axe label-content-name-mismatch and 12 slop markers (gradient text, glow stacks); A-3 had 2 axe violations and 7 eyebrow labels. All three B runs: 0 axe violations, 0 slop markers (fontFamilyCount 2 is informational). Judge preferred B in 2 of 3 pairs; the one A win was on hierarchy/clarity, with distinctiveness tied.

candidate_tuned.note: not run; the skill has no knobs

limits: n = 3 per arm; the +4 point primary delta rests on one run per arm hitting the same CSS bug, so the primary metric is a tie within noise.
Slop markers and the judge are secondary metrics designed for this trial (validated on a synthetic sloppy page and on both references), not an external standard.
Three judge calls by the same model family; blind to arm, but a model judge may share the skill's taste.
Token counts include each subagent's fixed context; only the A-B difference is meaningful. Wall time has shared-CPU noise (up to 12 concurrent agents).
verdict: WATCH (adopt for customer-facing UI if the visual signal matters): primary score tied within noise, but 0 slop markers and 0 axe violations in 3/3 skill runs vs 33 markers and 3 violations across the plain runs, judge 2:1 for the skill, at +8 % tokens and +18 % tool calls
reason: The functional score does not separate the arms (0.893 vs 0.933, each arm lost one run to the same CSS bug). The scripted secondary metrics do: every plain run shipped generic-AI markers (12, 14, 7) and two of three had axe violations; no skill run had either. Cost is modest (+8 % tokens, +0.4 % time).
